page: Microsoft Azure E128-32s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance within the Esv6 series running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel processor and is provisioned with 32 dedicated vCPUs alongside 1024.0 GB of system memory. This configuration yields a 1:32 compute-to-memory ratio, providing 32.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated hardware accelerators or discrete GPUs.

The hardware configuration includes no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached remote storage for filesystem and operational data persistence, with built-in capability for Premium Storage tiers. Dedicated vCPU allocation delivers consistent processing throughput without execution contention from co-located virtual machines. However, workloads requiring low-latency scratch space must account for the lack of local ephemeral drives. The instance also provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The high memory-to-vCPU ratio makes the E128-32s_v6 suitable for memory-dense operations where software licensing costs scale per core. The constrained 32-core allocation against a 1024.0 GB memory footprint improves resource efficiency when application performance depends on memory capacity rather than parallel CPU throughput. Primary target workloads include enterprise in-memory databases, large caching layers, and high-memory analytics processing.
description: Microsoft Azure E128-32s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 Intel architecture, operating on Microsoft Hyper-V. It provides 32 dedicated vCPUs and 1024.0 GB of system memory, delivering an extensive 32.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Designed for workloads with high memory consumption relative to computational requirements, this configuration lacks attached local storage and features zero integrated GPUs. Disk persistence is handled through external volumes, with compatibility for Premium Storage. The constrained core configuration allows organizations running database management systems, caching nodes, and enterprise in-memory data processing engines to utilize a terabyte of memory while minimizing per-core software licensing expenditures. Because no local solid-state drives or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are bundled with the hardware, all persistent storage operations and network routing rely entirely on supplementary cloud infrastructure services.
